questions.question:
**The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.**

They will go to bed / early since they / have to get up / at five on the morning.
questions.solution:
The erroneous part of the sentence is: **at five on the morning**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error here lies in the use of the preposition.
 
• Replace "**on**" with "**in**" to make the sentence correct.
 
• “**In**” and “**on**” are both time-based prepositions. We can use them in different ways when we want to talk about specific periods.
 
• We use **in **with morning, afternoon, evening and night when we are referring to a general time.
 
 
• **For example-** *I always work best in the morning.*
 
 
 
• But we use **on **when we talk about a specific morning, afternoon, etc., or when we describe the part of the day.
 
 
• **For example-** *On the morning of the 19th, I will have to rush to school.*
 
 
 
• The given sentence is talking about a general time in the morning, so the preposition "**in**" should be used here.
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is **option 2**, which contains the error in it.

**Corrected sentence:** *They will go to bed early since they have to get up at five in __the morning. *

questions.question: **Select the sentence with the appropriate use of prepositions. **

options.text: It has been raining till morning.
It has been raining from morning.
It has been raining by morning.
It has been raining since morning.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **It has been raining since morning.** 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

 
• Let us look at the meaning of the given prepositions.
 
 
• Till: Up to the point in time or the event mentioned. (समय तक या उल्लिखित घटना तक)
 
• From: Indicates the point in time at which a particular process, event, or activity starts. (उस समय को इंगित करना जिस पर एक विशेष प्रक्रिया, घटना या गतिविधि शुरू होती है)
 
• By: Identifies the agent performing an action. (कार्रवाई करने वाले एजेंट की पहचान करना)
 
• Since: From a particular time in the past until a later time, or until now. (अतीत में किसी विशेष समय से बाद के समय तक, या अब तक)
 
 
• **For example-** *I haven't eaten since breakfast.*
 
 
 
 
 
• The given sentence is saying that the rain has started in the morning and it is still continuing.
 
• We use since as a preposition, a conjunction and an adverb to refer to a time, and as a conjunction to introduce a reason.
 
• So, as per the meaning of the given prepositions "since" should be used here.

​Therefore, the correct answer is option 4.

• Rules of Conversion from Passive to Active Voice:
 
 
• Identify the subject, the verb, and the object.
 
• Change the object into the subject.
 
• Change the verb into the past participle form of the verb.
 
• Change the subject into an object.

questions.question:
**Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence.**

She said, “She must leave all the bad habits.”

options.text: She said she has to leave all the bad habits
She said that she must have leave all the bad habits
She said that she had to leave all the bad habits.
She said that she could leave all the bad habits

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **She said that she had to leave all the bad habits.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• The given sentence is in direct speech and we need to convert it to indirect speech.
 
• When we change a direct speech to an indirect speech, we must follow these rules:
 
 
• The reporting verb "said" remains unchanged in the indirect speech.
 
• The inverted commas ("...") are replaced with the conjunction 'that' to show the indirect speech part.
 
• The comma (,) is removed in the indirect speech.
 
• The first word of the indirect speech should be in capital letters.
 
• '**Must**' in direct speech changes to 'Had to' in indirect speech.
 
 
 
• Thus, option 3 is the correct answer.

 

Hence, indirect speech is - *She said that she had to leave all the bad habits.*

 

* [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__***

 
• **'MUST changes into HAD TO' from direct speech to indirect speech**

 
 
• He said, “I **must **study for the exam”. - He said that he had to study the exam.
 
• She said, “I **must **finish the work in time”.- She said that she had to finish the work in time.
